sources.title: Frederick Cooper, interview with Iva Peša and Alicia Schrikker, 2017 reprint
sources.citation: Iva Peša and Alicia Schrikker, Lessons from African History: between the deep and the shallow ends of social theory and historical empiricism. Interview with Frederick Cooper, in Carolien Stolte and Alicia Schrikker, eds., World History – a Genealogy (Leiden University Press, 2017), 337–352; interview conducted December 2013, first published Itinerario 38:3 (2014), 7–18, doi:10.1017/S0165115314000497.

verification.note: Read the complete Cooper interview 337–352, including all 24 notes, in the public publisher ebook retained from the Library of Congress; exact shared PDF hash recorded privately without changing the frozen Goody files. These are reprint locators, not original journal pagination. Publisher metadata verifies editors and 2017 edition. Neither the complete 430 page book nor original 2014 journal manifestation was newly read. Own answers are distinguished from interviewer questions and editorial bibliography. Woodward 1971 is a cited manifestation, and Davis 1975/da Costa 1985 cannot be assumed to predate his 1974 dissertation.

sources.title: Guillaume Vadot and Étienne Bourel, interview with Frederick Cooper, 2022
sources.citation: Guillaume Vadot and Étienne Bourel, Le travail, les idées et la question sociale dans l’histoire contemporaine de l’Afrique. Entretien avec Frederick Cooper, Cahiers d’études africaines 245–246 (2022): 41–61.

verification.note: Read complete original journal PDF 41–61 with metadata cover, 22 leaves, from its publisher. English email exchanges December 2021–February 2022 were translated into French by Vadot and Bourel and reviewed by Cooper in February 2022. The interview corrects a question’s implied early Du Bois influence, names Genovese and Capital, acknowledges Foucault, and compares the Burbank–Cooper project with Goody without proving influence. Its erroneous 1972 Roll, Jordan, Roll date is distinguished from the 1974 record in the 2017 witness/existing publisher record. Historical and disciplinary generalizations remain attributed, not independently adjudicated.

loc_cooper_category_2000.note: Fresh complete original Cambridge journal PDF 60–68 read, including all 18 notes. This permitted publisher reading confirms the earlier full-article record without silently extending it to cited books. Cooper’s praise and criticism of the joint Eley–Nield essay coexist; positive Eley/Blackbourn resource, Chakrabarty distinction, James/Trouillot complementary uses, Marx and Thompson’s categorical difficulty retain exact notes and coauthor/edition limits. Political and historical examples are Cooper’s analyses, not fresh archival validation.

loc_eley_nield_reply_2000.note: Fresh selected 76–83 read in the original Cambridge PDF, especially the complete Cooper response 81–83 through the agreement with his concluding task. Eley and Keith Nield share all reply credit. Their objections to his alleged distancing, experience, structures and agency coexist with substantial agreement. Later Scott discussion on 83 is not reassigned to Cooper. Prior selected 81–86 record remains; no new full 76–87 reading or original Cooper 1995 essay reading.
